meta.title: ci: skip expensive workflows on doc-only changes
meta.body_summary: Add paths-ignore filters to six CI workflow YAML files to skip expensive compilation, static analysis, and integration jobs for documentation-only PRs, reducing CI resource consumption and queue time.

perf_labels.notes: Codex-authored CI skip filter with ~4-line YAML changes per workflow, self-merged by maintainer after noting known CI false positive.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 28 lines distributed across 6 workflow YAML files, this is a tiny change by absolute volume. It fits a small-step, low-risk CI optimization and was merged without formal review.

review_details.concern_detail: No formal review feedback was provided; the only comment acknowledged a known false positive CI failure.
review_details.performance_claim: Skip expensive CI workflows for documentation-only PRs to reduce resource usage and CI queue times.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Codex managed straightforward YAML path filters; no technical stack boundary encountered. Merge required no additional evidence beyond author confidence.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No performance metrics or before/after CI duration data provided; the performance claim is narrative.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No regressions reported; known CI failure was dismissed as false positive.

core_change_summary.description: Added paths-ignore conditions for documentation paths (docs/**, *.md, etc.) to the trigger sections of multiple expensive CI workflows, preventing them from running when only doc files are changed.
change_trajectory: Single commit by rgerhards adding paths-ignore to six workflow YAMLs; no subsequent edits.
